Drone Reportedly Sinks Grain Ship Near Romania, Kills 2 — Two crew members died and 11 were rescued after the Turkey-owned grain carrier Royad Mammadov caught fire and sank near a Romanian offshore platform. On Monday, local media reported a possible drone strike, but Romanian authorities have not confirmed the cause or attributed the incident to Russia.

NATO Uses Lessons-Learned in Ukraine to Plan Russian Defeat in 3D+ Battlespace — NATO’s top commander in Europe is preparing a strategy for rapidly defeating a potential Russian attack on the alliance’s eastern flank, Bloomberg reported. The draft plan would use land forces alongside drones, minimally crewed systems and artificial intelligence to halt an incursion and destroy enemy command structures.

Hungary Set to Ease Ukraine EU Veto – But Only After Minority Rights Deal — Hungary is expected to stop blocking a procedural step that would advance Ukraine and Moldova’s EU accession talks, the Financial Times reported on Monday. However, opening the next two negotiation clusters would still depend on Ukraine’s parliament adopting a minority education bill on Oct. 12.

‘Kharkiv Defeated Putin’: Russian Bombs Kill Three a Day After Zelensky Praises City’s Defiance — Russian guided bombs and a drone hit Kharkiv, killing at least three people and wounding 29, including three children, as rescuers searched for people potentially trapped beneath a damaged apartment building.

Ukraine, Germany Sign €8.5B in Defense Deals, Merz Pledges More Air Defense Support — Ukraine and Germany signed 15 agreements worth over €8.5 billion covering joint weapons production, air defense, drones, and energy protection. The deals came as Merz visited Kyiv and reaffirmed Berlin’s military support despite growing political pressure at home.

Russia Repeatedly Tests Romanian Air Defense — Romania is investigating a suspected drone crash near Plauru during Russian attacks on neighboring Ukraine. The incident follows confirmed airspace violations elsewhere on NATO’s eastern flank and growing demands for stronger drone defenses.

Germany Could Be Pulled Into War With Russia, Intel Chiefs Warn — Germany risks being drawn into an armed conflict with Russia, the head of Germany’s foreign intelligence service warned on Oct. 5, describing Moscow’s activities against Germany and other NATO members as a growing “shadow war.” While Germany’s domestic intel boss says the Kremlin is willing to carry out sabotage and assassinations.

Russian Authorities Won’t Confirm Pneumonic Plague Outbreak in Central Siberia — Authorities in Russia’s Irkutsk region have expanded quarantine measures after the death of researcher Darya Shipilova following a reported laboratory accident involving pneumonic plague. India Moves to Broker Black Sea Deal Between Russia and Ukraine — India is holding talks with Russia and Ukraine on restoring safe navigation in the Black Sea as it seeks a more active role in efforts to end the war. ‘I Was a Skeptic’: Ukraine’s AI-Assisted Gun Turrets Shoot Down Russian Jet Drones — Ukraine says robotic machine-gun turrets using AI and machine vision have downed Russian jet-powered drones, including the Geran-5, as Kyiv expands deployments despite the systems’ limited range.

Europe’s Proposed Defense Union Would Put Ukraine at Its Core — MEPs are proposing a European Defense Union that would work alongside NATO while giving Europe greater capacity to act independently. The plan would involve Ukraine, Norway, and the UK, along with six institutions, including a security council and rapid reaction force.

Ukraine Is Running Out of Spare Locomotives as Russian Strikes Threaten Exports — Russian attacks have nearly exhausted Ukraine’s locomotive reserves, creating a bottleneck for grain and iron ore deliveries to Black Sea ports and prompting Kyiv to seek replacements from European partners.

Merz in Kyiv: Support Under Fire — German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s surprise Kyiv visit underscored Germany’s strong support for Ukraine, including €1 billion in military aid and €350 million for energy infrastructure. Estonian ‘Active Defense’ Strategy Seeks to Send Troops to Russian Border — The FT reports that the Estonian government is adopting a new defensive strategy laid out in its latest national security concept. Tallinn’s previous doctrine envisaged allowing attackers to enter the country before countering the enemy with a guerrilla-style defense to block Russian troops until NATO reinforcements arrived.

Russian Attack Sends Projectile Into Bus at Moldova Border — A projectile fell near Moldova’s Palanca-Maiaky-Udobne border crossing, ricocheted off the ground and struck a passenger bus. A Moldovan border guard was lightly wounded, and the crossing was temporarily closed.

‘We’re Staying’: European Embassies Defy Russia’s Warning to Leave Kyiv — European embassies are refusing to leave Kyiv despite Russian threats of further strikes, publicly reaffirming their support for Ukraine as Moscow seeks to intimidate foreign diplomats.

Kyiv Could Face 16-Hour Power Cuts, Expert Warns — Kyiv could face electricity cuts lasting 14-16 hours a day this month if Russia continues attacking facilities supplying the capital, utility expert Oleh Popenko warned. Three Russian Officers Linked to Missile Strikes on Ukraine Killed in Tu-95 Crash — Three Russian officers linked by a Ukrainian database to organizing missile strikes on Ukraine were among eight killed in a Tu-95MS bomber crash in Russia’s Amur Region on Sept. 29, independent Russian outlet Mediazona reported. All eight officers served in Russia’s strategic aviation forces, with three previously identified in Ukraine’s “Book of Executioners.”

White House Monitoring Reports Plague Case and Quarantine in Russia — The White House is monitoring reports of a suspected plague case in Russia after a 27-year-old institute worker died and 189 people were hospitalized following contact with her. Russian authorities have not confirmed the diagnosis, while a hospital in the Irkutsk region has been placed under quarantine.

Russia Upgrades Geran-4 Drones With Better Navigation and New Warhead, Ukraine Says — Russia has upgraded its Geran-4 attack drone with improved navigation, a new infrastructure-targeting warhead, and a Russian-made engine. Ukraine’s military intelligence says the changes could make the drone more accurate and less dependent on satellite navigation.

Bosnia Election Highlights Split Between Pro-Russian Dodik Camp and Ukraine Supporters — Pro-Russian politician Milorad Dodik’s SNSD retained its dominance in Republika Srpska, while three of the four leading parties in Bosnia’s Federation support Ukraine. The results underscore Bosnia’s political divisions and competing Russian and EU influence.

India Pushing for Bigger Role in Russia-Ukraine Talks — India is seeking a greater role in efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war, with talks covering Black Sea shipping, grain and energy exports and possible non-attack arrangements. Zelensky said the US hopes to broker a new round of negotiations by late October.

Russia’s Jet Drones Kill 1, Injure 8 in Kharkiv Amid 205-Drone Overnight Barrage — Russia launched 205 drones at Ukraine overnight, including 49 jet-powered Shahed-type UAVs. Three Banderol drones struck Kharkiv, killing one person and injuring eight, while Ukrainian air defenses shot down or suppressed 172 drones, the Air Force said.

Guterres’s Successor Will Need Russia’s Blessing — Seven candidates are competing to replace António Guterres amid demands for stronger international leadership. The alert follows a suspected arson attack against a Starlink facility in Poland and foiled sabotage at Leipzig Airport.

Ukrainian Mirage 2000 Downs Russian Cruise Missile With Cannon — A Ukrainian Air Force Mirage 2000-5F fighter jet intercepted and shot down a Russian S8000 Banderol compact cruise missile using its onboard 30mm DEFA 554 cannon, marking the first confirmed gun kill of the turbojet-powered munition by the French-supplied jet.

Russian Jet Drone Strikes Kyiv’s North Bridge, Injures 2 — A Russian jet-powered strike drone hit Kyiv’s North Bridge on Saturday morning, Oct. 3, damaging the road surface and overhead trolleybus lines and forcing the closure of westbound traffic across the Dnipro River, as well as injuring two people. The strike compounds mounting transit disruption following earlier attacks that shut the South Bridge, alongside overnight ballistic strikes that killed one person.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 2, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on November 2, 2026.

Russian Ballistic Missiles and Drones Hit Kyiv, Killing 1 — Kyiv came under another combined Russian ballistic missile and drone attack early Saturday, with one person killed, two wounded and fires reported in several districts.

Stubb: Every Russian Threat Should Bring More Support for Ukraine — Finnish President Alexander Stubb said Russia’s hybrid pressure on Europe should result in more support for Ukraine, while Maia Sandu and Volodymyr Zelensky warned that Moscow’s threat extends well beyond the current war.

Sandu: Russia Will Remain Major Threat to Europe Even After Ukraine War Ends — Maia Sandu warned that Russia’s threat to Europe will persist beyond the war in Ukraine, calling for stronger European defenses, accountability and faster EU enlargement.

Ukraine Records Nearly 227,000 Russian War Crimes Since Full-Scale Invasion — Ukraine’s National Police has opened nearly 244,000 criminal proceedings linked to Russia’s invasion, including 226,766 war crimes cases and 153 involving sexual violence.

Russian Drone Strikes Fire-Rescue Unit in Zaporizhzhia Region, Wounding Rescuer — Ukraine’s emergency service said Russian forces deliberately targeted a fire-rescue unit in Zaporizhzhia region, injuring one rescuer.

Russia Plans Record $200B Defense Budget as Healthcare, Education, Face Cuts — Russia’s 2027 draft budget includes a sharp increase in military spending while reducing planned healthcare, education and social expenditures, highlighting the growing fiscal cost of the war.

Putin Ally Schröder Takes Russian Business Post After Kremlin Floated Him as Ukraine Mediator — Gerhard Schröder has joined the supervisory board of Russian retailer Hyperglobus, deepening his ties to Moscow after the Kremlin repeatedly presented him as a potential mediator over Ukraine.

Zelensky: Putin’s Goal Is Not Donbas but All of Ukraine — Volodymyr Zelensky said Vladimir Putin’s latest rhetoric shows Moscow’s ambitions extend beyond Donbas to all of Ukraine and warned that Russia also seeks renewed influence over neighboring states.
